# Messages

<!-- GENERATED by Scripts/gen_messages_doc.py from the compilers' sources: do not edit by hand. -->

Every message the tools print, in English, as the code writes it, with
`<n>` for a number, `<name>` for a name or a text and `<x>` for a
value. What the common ones mean and how to get past them is in
[Messages](../messages.md).

## cmmcomp (C±)

## asmcomp

### Errors

- Error: out of memory while growing the symbol table!
- Error: where the heck is the file <name>?
- Error: couldn't open the file '<name>' for the life of me!!
- Error: couldn't create the file <name>/app\_log.txt.
- Error: the constant '<name>' is not a number.
- Error: the constant <name> does not fit the processor's float (NBMANT <n>, NBEXPO <n>): its exponent is past the maximum.
- Error: #NUGAIN <n> does not fit a signed <n>-bit word (at most <n>): norm(x), which is x / NUGAIN, would divide by a negative number. Use a smaller #NUGAIN.
- Error: #NUGAIN <n> is not a power of two. norm(x) is x / NUGAIN in hardware: a power of two becomes a shift (~12 LUT levels); anything else becomes a constant divider (38 to 70 levels, measured), the critical path of the whole ALU.
- Error: floating-point setup doesn't add up. You gotta have NUBITS = NBMANT + NBEXPO + 1 (NUBITS <n>, NBMANT <n>, NBEXPO <n> add up to <n>). A program without float needs no #NBMANT or #NBEXPO.
- Error: the exponent is too short for the mantissa (NBMANT <n>, NBEXPO <n>). You need NBMANT < 2^(NBEXPO-1): with no hidden bit, 1.0 is 2^(NBMANT-1) x 2^-(NBMANT-1), and that exponent has to fit. Widen NBEXPO or narrow NBMANT.
- Error: #NUBITS <n> is past 32. A SAPHO word is at most 32 bits.
- Error: <name> <name>: the operand of LDI/ILI/STI/ISI is an array name or an integer base address.
- Error: <name> takes <n> words: it must be followed by <n> NOP and the read of its result (expected <name>, found <name>). The compilers write the sequence; in a hand-written .asm, write it out.
- Error: the operand of <name> is the link number, an integer from 0 to <n> (found '<name>').
- Error: #LKSYNC <n>, but the program has no TOM or CAD on link <n>.
- Error: the program ends inside the sequence of <name> (NOPs and <name> are missing).
- Error: #FROUND only takes 0 (legacy), 1 (truncation + saturation) or 2 (round to nearest even).
